lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Julie, how's your day?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I was looking for jobs today. I think I need to get a job.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: I see. I hope you do. How about you, Soyeong?

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: I don't have any plans for the weekend yet. So, Julie, are you going to keep track of things this weekend?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: No, I'm not. I don't want to search for jobs on weekend.

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: I'm with you. Julie.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: I agree. Yu-Jin says there is a cherry blossom road nearby. The cherry blossoms are in full bloom this weekend. I'm planning to visit there. Do you want to go see them together?

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: Great idea! I'll take you to the places.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Wow, thanks. I saw cherry blossoms blooming in front of the guesthouse. It was so beautiful. I've never actually seen cherry blossoms before.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Me, too. It looks like snow. When the wind blows, it feels like it's snowing. If we go to Cherry Blossom Road, we will probably see the scene.

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: I'm looking forward to it. I'll take my camera. It will be a good chance to take a picture.
[Understagram Contents]

Yesterday, cherry blossom road. In full bloom ATM. The cherry blossoms fell like snow. BTW, there were so many people. Hard to take pics. Noble Restaurant was really good. If you wanna go there, you should make a reservation B4 you go. Need some information about the restaurant or the street? AMA.
#Korea #Seoul #Cherryblossomstreet #noblerestaurant #pasta #withHarry

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Julie, what are you doing?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I'm putting my pictures on Understagram now.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Understagram?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Yes. It's one of the well-known social media. Like a photo album, you can upload pictures and record them. It's easy to see and I can give news to my friends.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Oh, interesting. I haven't used it yet. Can you teach me?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Sure. You will learn it quickly. First, you need to download the app on your cell phone and log in. It's your first time using it, so let's sign up.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Let me see.... Like this? I joined.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Then you can select the pictures in the library and comment on them. It is a good way to add hashtags as well. Press Upload to finish. Look, the picture's up, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Oh, it looks like an album. I think it's easy to use.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Yes, we can now follow each other.

topic: Lesson 5 - On the Way to the Library

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Good morning Yu-Jin. Where are you going?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Hi, Julie. My husband and I are going to the city library to borrow books. Oh, are you guys new to each other, right? This is Min-Su, my husband.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Hi, I'm Julie. Nice to meet you. I've heard a lot from Yu-Jin. Are you back from your business trip?

lines.speaker: Min-Su
lines.text: Nice to meet you, too. How are you? I'm fine, thank you. Yes, I'm back.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Oh, Min-Su... He only learned English from textbooks. And... he loves Konglish.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Konglish? That sounds interesting! While I stay here, we'll get to know each other, and your English will improve for sure. By the way, I want to go to the library. Can I join you?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Of course. Get in the car. It will take a few minutes.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Yeah! Let's go to the library!

lines.speaker: Min-Su
lines.text: Let's go. Oh, I need to adjust the position of the back mirror.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Back mirror? What's the back mirror?

lines.speaker: Min-Su
lines.text: "Back mirror." The mirror in front of the driver's seat.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Oh, you mean "Rear View Mirror"?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Wow, is the "back mirror" Konglish? Rear view mirror? In Korea, most people use the term "back mirror" instead of "rear view mirror."

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: It is interesting to hear the different usage of English expression between Korea and the States.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Soyeong, InSung, your English pronunciation is really good.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Right. You seem to be a native English speaker, Soyeong.

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: Thanks. I used to live in the States.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I want to know the ways to maintain or improve your English. The tips will help me when I teach English to my students. How do you practice English pronunciation?

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: I have been watching English classes on OUN-TV and American TV shows with English subtitles.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: That's a good idea.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Well, in my case, I didn't have enough time to watch TV because of my job. So I listen to lots of English programs through my smartphone while I'm on the bus or subway.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Ah, yes! That's the best way to use your time when you are commuting. What else?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: I also try to learn by reading online newspapers and magazines in English. Above all things, it helps to make friends with English speakers.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: See? I contributed a lot to your English, guys.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Come on, that's what friends are for.
[The way to the guest house]

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Look at the school over there. What makes so many people stand in front of the school?

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: I think that is because today is Teacher's Day. The teachers and students are standing to greet each other.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Oh, Korea has Teacher's Day, too.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: There is Teacher's Day in America, too, right? When is Teacher's Day in America?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: In the United States, the first full week of May is Teacher Appreciation Week. National Teacher Day is on Tuesday during the week. It is May 10 this year.

lines.speaker: Soyeong
lines.text: It's amazing to have "Teacher's Week". We have Teacher's Day on May 15th. Harry, how about the UK?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: We annually celebrate World Teacher's day also known as International Teacher's Day. It is October 5.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: I see. It's been a while. I think I should call my high school teacher.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Oh, your teacher will be very pleased.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: So, Julie, where are you planning to go today?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I'm going to go to Insadong. I heard that it is a traditional Korean marketplace. I will get something for my family there. It's a great place to shop for souvenirs, but it's quite crowded there, right?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Yes, it's really busy. How about you, Justin? How are you going to get there?

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: I get there by bus and transfer to the subway, or I can take a taxi. I will take a bus and subway to sightsee Seoul.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Oh, that's a good idea. Buses and subways will not be very crowded at this time.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I heard that I need a transportation card to transfer. Where can I get a transportation card?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: You can buy it at banks, subway booths, and bus stops. If you don't mind, shall I go together with you guys?

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Of course not! It's a relief that you can go with us.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Do you have anything to buy?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Actually, my husband will come back from his business trip soon. So I want to prepare a gift for him.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Wow, you are so sweet.

topic: Lesson 9 - Shopping and Getting a Refund

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Harry, what are you doing here? What are all these shopping bags?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: These are all clothes. I looked around downtown and saw many nice clothes. I bought the clothes I'm wearing, too. And it's trendy this season. Isn't that cool?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Yeah, looks good. So, you bought all these today?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: I was planning to go window shopping, but I bought them all. And... yes. As I told you, I seem to have made many impulse purchases today. I've spent almost all of my budget for the trip today.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Oh, Harry. What do you want to do now?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: I'd better get a refund on these. I'll go back to the guesthouse and tell what is needed and what is not.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I think that's a good idea. How long does the refund take? I mean I'm wondering till when you can get a refund.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Let's see... It says on the receipt that a refund is possible within 15 days of the purchase date.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Harry, your decision will make the rest of the trip more satisfying.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: That's comforting to know! Thank you.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: I think my hair is too long. I'd like to change my hairstyle. InSung, do you have any hair shops you recommend?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: There is a hair shop that I often go to. Do you want to go with me? It is quite famous.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Oh, good. Let's go!
[At the hair shop]

lines.speaker: Hairdresser
lines.text: Welcome. What kind of hairstyle do you want?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: My hair is too long. I'd like to trim it, and what's the latest style?

lines.speaker: Hairdresser
lines.text: Two-block cut is in fashion.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: What's a two-block cut?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Undercut is a two-block cut.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Oh, the undercut doesn't suit me. I think I'd better get my hair cut or trimmed.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: People dye their hair bright these days. Why don't you dye it too?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: I'll just get a trim today.

lines.speaker: Hairdresser
lines.text: Okay, I'll get started.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: This is D-Mart. It looks like Price-co.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Why don't we eat something first at the food court here?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: That's a good idea. I just happen to be very hungry.
[On the food court]

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: There are many different kinds of food. Should we choose what we want to eat, or should we order all together at one restaurant?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: You can order what you want. You can pay for Korean, Chinese, Western, or Japanese food here. And order fast food in front of the store. I'm going to order pork cutlet.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: I'd better eat bibimbap. Julie, what about you?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I want to try gimbap. I saw it as I passed by before, and it looks very delicious.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Gimbap goes well with ramen. Why don't you try the set menu?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I prefer udon to ramen. Ramen was too spicy for me.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: There is also the gimbap and udon set. I'll eat fast food. I'll go and get the order.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Okay. Let's meet again at this table.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I'm totally into gimbap. I think it's the best Korean food I've ever eaten.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Gimbap is easy to make when the ingredients are ready. Julie, would you like to make it?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Oh, are you taking Yu-Jin's Korean cooking classes?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Do you want to join us, Harry?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: That would be great.
[In the kitchen]

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: I've chopped all the ingredients, and now I'm going to fry them. You have to fry all the ingredients.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: Okay. I'll fry them.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Thanks, Harry. Then, place the seaweed on the bamboo roller mat and spread the seasoned rice on top of it. Cover with a thin layer of rice as if spreading butter. Place the fried ingredients on top of the rice.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Oh, I think I know what to do next. You will roll this up, right?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Exactly. Cut the rolled gimbap and it's complete.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Why don't we talk over dinner together?

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Great. There's a good pizza place nearby. How about going there?

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: InSung said that there is a delivery app. I want to try it.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Oh, you can order pizza using a delivery app. If you're interested in delivered food, let's try it tonight!

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Great! It's wonderful to have pizza delivered. How do I order?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Open the app and select the pizza category. Then it will show you the names, menus, photos and prices of various restaurants. You just check the menu of a restaurant and call!

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: I'll take our order then. What kind of pizza do you prefer?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I like them all. But the shrimp potato pizza looks really delicious.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: That looks good. I'll also take this one.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Okay.
[On the phone]

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Hello. This is the English Guesthouse, 123-gil, Seoul-ro. I'd like to order a large shrimp potato pizza. Add garlic sauce, please. And a 15L of Coke, too. I'll pay by credit card.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: So, all we have to do is wait for the pizza?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: The pizza will arrive in about half an hour. Why don't we set the table?

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Julie, why do you look so sick?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Is it that obvious? I feel like throwing up. I met my friend for dinner last night, and I have a stomachache.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Have you tried medicine?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: No, I didn't take it because I thought it would be okay, but it keeps hurting.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: I think you'd better go to see a doctor. I'll go to the hospital with you.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Then let's take my car and go together.
[At the hospital]

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Hi Julie, I understand that you're not feeling well. Where does it hurt?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Maybe the food I had last night was spoiled. I have been having diarrhea and I have no energy.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: I think it's enteritis. Don't eat anything for a day if you can. Have a little of the soup if you feel better.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: You'd better get some rest today.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Yes, Yu-Jin, InSung, thank you very much. When I woke up in the morning, I was in so much pain.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin and Min-Su
lines.text: Congratulations!

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: We're really glad you got the job you wanted. We're sad that you're leaveing, but it's really good for you.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Thank you for everything. I was very lucky to meet you. I couldn't have done this without you.

lines.speaker: Yu-Jin
lines.text: Don't mention it. Here, we brought you something. It's just a little something. I hope you like it.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Aw, You really shouldn't have. Ah, a Korean conversation book! This is exactly what I've been looking for. Thanks!
[Doorbell rings; Min-Su opens the door; Harry and InSung appear smiling.]

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: We're not late, are we? Congratulations on your job, Julie.

lines.speaker: InSung
lines.text: Here's a present for you.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I can't believe it. Thanks, guys! I'm so sorry to say goodbye to you.

lines.speaker: Harry
lines.text: We can keep in touch and meet anytime. Let's see how we are doing* through social media as well.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Absolutely.
